real_errors.title: R10_VALIDATION section 1 says 'None of the pairs below fires the match by itself' and owner row 2 says 'Firing still needs a second fault at Q124'; both are false for PYRO1_OUT to 3V3 (R173.1-D120.3, 0.5135 mm) and to 3V3A (R164.2, 0.5662 mm), and row 2's sentence is also false for the OUT-to-GND residuals it lists
real_errors.evidence: Geometry (pcbnew, .supervisor/r26_triage/adjacent.py -> adj_pyro1_out.out, board 92c3ad59): PYRO1_OUT R173.1 B(16.87,59.27) to 3V3 D120.3 B(15.7,60.2) 0.5135 mm B.Cu; PYRO1_OUT track (15.5,56.6)-(16.87,57.97) to 3V3A R164.2 (16.5,55.9) 0.5662 mm B.Cu (rounded-rect corner); also PYRO1_OUT-GND 0.1768 / 0.1800 mm, PYRO1_OUT-3V3 via (9.2,52.98) 0.620 mm on F.Cu, BUZZ_G 0.510 mm (no fire, mA). Circuit (board netlist): RAW_ACT -> R134 2 R -> J121.2 -> match -> J121.1 = PYRO1_OUT -> Q124 drain; cold pull-up 3V3 -> D120 (BAT54A, anode pin 3) -> R131 10 k -> PYRO1_OUT; CONT and BUS dividers 11.2 k (5.1 k + 5.1 k over 2 k || 2 k); R164 2.2 R from 3V3 to 3V3A. Cold screen (PC1 and PE4 low; Calculation): healthy CONT / BUS 96.2-99.4 / 96.1-99.3 mV (Vf 0.3-0.2 V), open CONT 141.5-146.2 mV / BUS 0; with a bridge present at power-up PYRO1_OUT = 3.3 V, so CONT = BUS = 3.3 / 11.2 = 0.295 V (open match: CONT 0.295 V, BUS 0), 2.96x healthy and 2.0x open, and the match carries <= 0.29 mA (3.3 V into the 11.2 k bus divider; Q120 / Q121 body diodes back-to-back): the mandated CONT-upper / BUS bands (F8, M3_R10 Firmware 'any ground fault is a hard refusal before PC1', R19-SAF-04) refuse before PC1. Any bridge able to fire (< about 10 ohm) reads this way. Procedure: after per-flight step 5 closes J400 on the rail with the e-match in, the board powers up, runs the cold screen (>= 1 s, rule 2) and raises PC1, and 'the accepted single-switch design leaves the bus enabled from the on-rail check until the switch is opened' (M3_R10 Firmware) or LANDED (rule 6): pad wait and flight. Step 3 raises PC1 only with the 1-2 ohm dummy. A bridge that forms after PC1 is high is not screened: with 3V3 held at 3.3 V the match carries (7.4-8.4 - 3.3) V over a 2.8-4.5 ohm loop (R134 1.97-2.03, match 0.73-2.0, leads 0-0.3, FETs and copper) = about 0.9-1.8 A against the J-Tek 0.75 A all-fire; AP63203 does not sink in PFM (DS41326 Rev 3-2, 'Pulse Frequency Modulation'), so otherwise the rail is driven past U1's 4.0 V absolute maximum (I-5). For 3V3A the loop adds R164 2.2 R: about 0.6-1.0 A until R164 (0603, 0.8-2.3 W) opens, then VDDA / U4 / U5 over-voltage. So the section 1 table rows (lines 2354-2355: 'about 0.3-0.8 A') and the J440.1 / J440.2 harness row (line 2363: 'Joins the existing OUT-to-GND fire class') contradict line 2340's summary; row 2 (line 2169) covers 'the fire path' and its residual list (lines 2218-2219) includes the OUT-GND approaches that line 2340 itself says fire an enabled match. FMEA I-5 (R10) and owner row 1 omit the two pairs.
real_errors.severity_reasoning: Minor, not Critical / Major. The defect a 0.51 mm pad pair can carry from assembly (a bridge present at power-up) cannot fire: the cold screen reads 0.295 V against 0.099 V and refuses before PC1. A bridge that forms after PC1 is high (pad wait or flight) can fire, but that later-fault case is the single-string class the records already put to the owner: line 2340's own first sentence, owner row 1 ('Q124 and the firmware that drives it alone keep the e-match from firing'; row 18 is the pad lever) and FMEA I-5; its disclosed members are more likely (OUT-GND 0.177 / 0.180 mm, Q124 gate-drain 0.520 mm per R25 triage, C128 at 991 microstrain, In2 3V3 0.300 mm from RAW_PROTECTED over 132 mm); R173, D120, R164 and their copper are in the mandatory coat selection (ORDERING 8.3); the R10 fault model is single-string (FMEA line 58, F8, owner decision 2026-10-28). The board breaks no AGENTS section 2 rule or stated requirement; the error is that the record denies two members of a disclosed class.
real_errors.concrete_fix: Text only. (1) R10_VALIDATION line 2340: replace 'None of the pairs below fires the match by itself.' with 'Rows below that put PYRO1_OUT onto a lower-potential net also fire an enabled match by themselves: PYRO1_OUT to 3V3 (R173.1-D120.3, 0.5135 mm, B.Cu) and to 3V3A (the track (15.5,56.6)-(16.87,57.97) to R164.2, 0.5662 mm, B.Cu) drive the bus through R134 and the match into the rail (about 0.9-1.8 A if the rail held 3.3 V; otherwise past U1's 4.0 V, the I-5 mechanism), and the J440.1 / J440.2 harness row joins the OUT-to-GND class; QSPI_IO2-PE4 needs a sustained IO2-high pattern; the other rows cannot. A bridge present at power-up reads CONT = BUS = 0.295 V cold (healthy 0.099 V, open CONT 0.146 V) and is refused before PC1; one that forms after PC1 is high is not screened (owner row 18 covers the pad).' (2) Owner row 2: 'For the load-switch, PC1 enable-chain, EN-node and sense-branch defects firing still needs a second fault at Q124; the PYRO1_OUT residuals (GND 0.177 / 0.180 mm, 3V3 0.5135 mm, 3V3A 0.5662 mm) fire an enabled match by themselves (row 1).' (3) Owner row 1 and FMEA I-5 (R10): add 'a PYRO1_OUT bridge to GND, 3V3 or 3V3A' (bus voltage onto 3V3 / 3V3A through the match). (4) Respin list: PYRO1_OUT >= 1 mm from 3V3 / 3V3A (D120 about 0.55 mm west; R164 about 0.45 mm north or the diagonal re-drawn); a GND guard is not a fix at PYRO1_OUT (GND is foreign there, S-8), and H-9's 3V3 clamp does not close these routes (a clamped rail lets about 1 A through the match). No new refusal rule is needed: the existing CONT-upper / BUS bands refuse a pre-existing bridge at about 3x the healthy reading. A board-spacing change is an owner respin option: it would close two members of a class whose closer OUT-GND members remain, and restart the clean-round count.

real_errors.title: 'An adversarial search over 4000 trains under 7.62 ms per window kept EN >= 1.1173 V' is a sampled result, not the worst case: the admissible one-block-per-100 ms train reaches 1.1162 V at 7.62 ms and 1.1168 V on the search's own 0.1 ms grid (7.6 ms)
real_errors.evidence: en_model.py (same corner as R26-TRI-02) at 5.73 V: one open block of 7.6199 ms at the end of every 100 ms, from closed steady state, EN after blocks 1 / 2 / 3 / 12 = 1.13050 / 1.11716 / 1.11629 / 1.11623 V; 7.6 ms (76 x 0.1 ms, the budget of .supervisor/r25_triage/window_rule.py, Xn = int(0.999 x 7.6287 / 0.1)) gives 1.11677 V < 1.1173 V. Every sliding 100 ms window of that train holds exactly the block length. Exchange argument: with the affine open / closed maps O(v) = vo + (v - vo)a and C(v) = vc + (v - vc)b, C(O(v)) - O(C(v)) = (1 - a)(1 - b)(vc - vo) > 0, so moving open time later lowers EN and the latest packing (one block per 100 ms) is the worst admissible train. The 7.629 ms limit itself is right. Quoted in REQUIREMENTS F6 (line 60), M3_R10 line 270, ORDERING 8.3 line 617, R10_VALIDATION row 21, r10_sch_check.py line 295 -> binding note line 589, D-R25-01 (line 4251); STATUS line 19 names the search.

observations.reason: Not a real error: DS41326 Rev 3-2 section 10 ties the saturation rating to the operating peak (ILOAD + dIL/2, Eq. 8) and asks for a DC rating >= 1.35 x the maximum load, not Isat above the 2.5-3.1 A HS limit; the 3V3 operating peak is about 0.6-0.85 A (dIL about 0.48 A at 8.4 V, 1.1 MHz, 3.76 uH) against 2.90 A, and no record claims a fault-current rating for L1.
